name: 1 & 2 Samuel

objectives.text: Retell how God called the boy Samuel in the night and how Samuel answered, "Speak, for your servant hears"
Retell how David trusted the Lord to fight for him when he faced Goliath
Retell how Hannah prayed to the Lord for a son and gave Samuel back to serve the Lord
Identify Saul as Israel's first king and David as the king the Lord chose and Samuel anointed to replace him
Explain what the Lord's words to Samuel in 1 Samuel 16:7 teach about how God chose David
Describe the covenant friendship of David and Jonathan using examples from the text
Describe how David showed kindness to Mephibosheth because of his promise to Jonathan
Explain why Israel's request for a king like all the nations displeased Samuel and the Lord
Explain why David refused to harm Saul when he had the chance, using David's own words
Compare Saul's response to Samuel's rebuke with David's response to Nathan's rebuke
Explain what Samuel meant when he told Saul that to obey is better than sacrifice
Outline the structure of 1 and 2 Samuel around the careers of Samuel, Saul, and David
Describe how David united the tribes, made Jerusalem his capital, and brought the ark into the city
Analyze what the capture of the ark and the death of Uzzah reveal about the holiness of God and the danger of treating his presence as a tool
Analyze the promises the Lord made to David in the Davidic covenant concerning his house, his offspring, and his throne
Trace how David's sin with Bathsheba led to the consequences Nathan announced within David's own family
Analyze how the New Testament presents Jesus Christ as the fulfillment of the promise to David of an everlasting king
Analyze the contrast between kingship under God's law and kingship like that of the nations as presented in Samuel
Evaluate the character of Absalom and David's response to his rebellion using evidence from the narrative
Analyze the role of the prophets Samuel, Nathan, and Gad in confronting and holding Israel's kings accountable to the word of the Lord
Evaluate scholarly theories about the composition of Samuel, such as the Court History or Succession Narrative, in light of the Reformed doctrine of Scripture's inspiration and authority
Compose an essay tracing the messianic themes that frame 1 and 2 Samuel in the Song of Hannah and the last words of David

changes: Kept and reworded the real competencies: Samuel's call, David and Goliath, Saul and David as kings, God looking at the heart, Saul versus David's response to rebuke, David and Jonathan, the Davidic covenant, the ark, Bathsheba and its family consequences, unification under David, theocratic versus monarchical rule, Absalom, composition theories, and the Song of Hannah and David's last words. Dropped the feeling-based 'David loved God with all his heart' and the 'best king' judgment, and replaced the vague 'apply the lesson of friendship' with a text-based description. Reframed 'transition from Judges to Kings' as Israel's request for a king in 1 Samuel 8 to keep it within Samuel. Recast the historiography item as an evaluation in light of the Reformed doctrine of Scripture. Added Hannah's prayer, kindness to Mephibosheth, David sparing Saul, obedience over sacrifice, an outline of the books, New Testament fulfillment of the Davidic covenant, and the prophets' role in confronting kings. Expanded verse anchors, kept WCF 7.3 on the covenant objective, and added catechism references on Christ's kingly office and confession articles on Scripture.
